what: How each Texas place voted in five contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic candidate or ticket, the Republican candidate or ticket, everyone else together (write-ins included) and the total, added up from the Texas Legislative Council's election returns by voting tabulation district, which it compiles from the counties' and the Secretary of State's returns.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, in the Texas Legislative Council's returns by voting tabulation district (the census-drawn match of each county's election precincts), added up here by county, by judicial and court of appeals district (whole counties), and for 2022 and 2024 by state House, state Senate and State Board of Education district on the plans still in force for 2026. The Council's figures are not the certified canvass: statewide, the Democratic and Republican counts differ from the official ones by 0.04 percent or less, and its write-in line counts more write-ins than the official figures do; each difference is stated in the file. Where a precinct lay in two districts the Council divided its votes by estimate, so such a district is left out for that year: nothing here is divided by estimate. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a district's figures are for its lines of that year. The candidates and tickets are named only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted, so there the split is left out.

few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are kept here all the same, so that the sums can be checked.

not_given: Cities and towns are not added up: the Council's returns do not say which city a precinct lies in, and no Texas race in these lists is a city's. County commissioners, justice of the peace and constable precincts are not added up: each Texas election precinct lies wholly inside one of each, but no statewide list a script can read says which. School, hospital and other districts are not added up, and neither are congressional districts (the 2026 plan was not in force at these elections).

house.what: State House districts of PLANH2316, the plan in force for 2022, 2024 and 2026
house.why_not: A district is missing in a year when a precinct of it lay partly in another district, or when a district contest's votes fell outside the district's VTDs: the Council divided such a precinct's votes by estimate, and nothing is divided by estimate here. The 2020 election was held on the districts of the 2010s; the plans drawn after the 2020 census were first used in 2022, so 2020 is not given.
house.note: A district is its VTDs added up, as the Council's RED-110 report for PLANH2316 lists them for each election's VTDs. Each district contest the Council's data carries (contested races only) was checked: its votes must fall only in its own district's VTDs.
